v.rationale: The three are nearly identical in core logic. Each has the same #[Scope] inactiveFor with grouped whereNull/orWhere, a nullable timestamp migration, an attribute-based command, and Schedule::command()->dailyAt('06:00')->appendOutputTo(). All suites pass. The probes (--days=0, a huge value, an empty string, whitespace, the output text) found no crashes. impl-2 deliberately rejects --days=0. Small differences decided the ranking. impl-1 ranks first: it uses the modern $this->fail(), freezes time globally, and is the only one whose schedule test checks the log output destination, which is the 'shows up in our logs' requirement. Its weakness is loose ': 1' containment assertions. impl-3 is equally clean, with a factory state, exact output assertions and components->error, but its schedule test skips the log destination and it includes a low-value schema test. impl-2 ranks last. It hardcodes an unrequested Europe/Copenhagen timezone on the schedule, leaves a duplicate commented RefreshDatabase line in Pest.php, prints the ungrammatical '1 users', and uses MySQL-only ->after(). Otherwise its tests are thorough.
